title: Apple stock App Store growth slows in June, UBS maintains neutral rating
content:
Investing.com - UBS maintained its Neutral rating and $210.00 price target on Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) stock after analyzing recent App Store performance data. According to InvestingPro data, Apple currently trades at a premium valuation with high EBITDA and revenue multiples, while analyst targets range from $173 to $300.

The investment firm reported that App Store growth slowed approximately 70 basis points month-over-month to about 10% on a foreign exchange neutral basis in June, according to data from Sensor Tower. This comes as Apple’s overall revenue growth reached 4.9% in the last twelve months, with the company maintaining strong profitability metrics and an impressive return on assets of 29.1%.

On a reported basis, growth reached approximately 12% as the U.S. dollar weakened during the quarter, UBS noted in its analysis.

Growth rates were relatively consistent between the United States (approximately 12%) and the rest of the world (approximately 13%) on a reported basis, though the comparative baselines differed significantly at roughly 18% in the U.S. versus approximately 10% in other markets.

Looking ahead to the September quarter, UBS indicated that Apple faces a comparison baseline of roughly 12%, which is one percentage point easier than the June quarter comparison. With earnings scheduled for July 31st, InvestingPro offers 14 additional key insights about Apple’s financial health and market position, available in the comprehensive Pro Research Report.

In other recent news, Apple has been at the center of several notable developments. KeyBanc has maintained its Sector Weight rating on Apple, adjusting its quarterly estimates based on spending data. The firm raised its fiscal third-quarter estimates above consensus but lowered its fiscal fourth-quarter projections. Meanwhile, Evercore ISI reiterated an Outperform rating and a $250 price target on Apple despite the departure of a key AI executive, Ruoming Pang, who left for Meta (NASDAQ:META). The leadership changes in Apple’s AI division have reportedly impacted team morale, yet Evercore ISI views Apple’s AI strategy as flexible and cost-conscious.

Goldman Sachs has also maintained its Buy rating and a $253 price target on Apple, despite challenges in the Chinese smartphone market. Data showed a 10% year-over-year decline in foreign-branded phone shipments in China, though Apple managed to increase its market share through strategic discounting. Additionally, Apple has filed a legal challenge against a $587 million fine imposed by the European Union for allegedly breaching the Digital Markets Act. The company argues that the EU’s decision oversteps legal requirements and plans to contest the ruling in court.

title: Sundial Raises $23M to Redefine Data-informed Decisions with AI
content:
Led by DJ Patil at GPV, Sundial’s Series A fuels its vision to turn every decision-maker into their own expert analyst.

SAN FRANCISCO, July 08, 2025--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sundial, the AI-powered analytics platform redefining how companies make decisions, today announced it has raised a total of $23 million, including a recent $16 million Series A funding round led by GPV partner DJ Patil, the first-ever U.S. Chief Data Scientist and a pioneer in data science.

"Sundial is the only data company focused on reducing the time to quality decisions—not just serving up charts, but guiding action," said DJ Patil, GPV Partner and Sundial board member. "This team pioneered the growth and data practices at Facebook; they took that expert know-how and combined it with cutting-edge AI to build something revolutionary."

In a market crowded with fragmented analytics tools—dashboards, notebooks, data transformation pipelines—Sundial unifies these capabilities into one intuitive platform. By combining AI with expert analytical frameworks, Sundial helps anyone in an organization make smarter, faster decisions.

Julie Zhuo, co-founder and former VP of Design at Meta, said: "We built Sundial to democratize analytics so that anyone—from product to engineering to GTM to finance—can understand and act on critical data without needing a data science degree."

Chandra Narayanan, co-founder and former Chief Analytics Officer at Sequoia Capital and Instagram, added: "Leaders don’t need more data—they need better insights. Using agentic workflows married with deep analytical expertise, we can deliver complex analyses that have never before been automated to help companies zero in on the biggest opportunities."

Sundial has attracted funding from notable investors and firms including Sequoia Capital, Sunflower Capital, Slow Ventures, Unusual Ventures, Tribe Capital, Electric Capital, and prominent industry luminaries such as Fidji Simo, Tobi Lütke, Alex Schultz, Drew Houston, Amjad Masad, Shishir Mehrotra, Deb Liu, Howie Liu, Anil Varanasi, Ruchi Sanghvi, Brian Hale, Jay Parikh, and Javier Olivan.

Sundial’s analytics platform has already demonstrated significant value for Fortune 500 companies and fast-growing AI start-ups. David Sasaki, VP of Analytics and Insights at OpenAI said: "Sundial automated complex data engineering tasks that would have taken our small team months to build internally. We went from raw logging to comprehensive data visibility virtually overnight."

With this investment, Sundial will expand its engineering and product teams, invest in core AI capabilities, and scale adoption among companies seeking faster, more actionable insights in an AI-first era.

title: Why Goldman Sachs and BofA lifted their S&P 500 targets
content:
Goldman Sachs (GS) analysts lift their S&P 500 (^GSPC) target to 6,600 from 6,100, citing Federal Reserve rate cuts, bond weakness, and investors' willingness to look past near-term challenges. Bank of America (BAC) analysts also increased their target, but see little upside from current levels.

Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Allie Canal outlines the top calls on Wall Street and takes a closer look at valuation in the Big Tech sector, including names like Nvidia (NVDA), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), and Meta (META).

To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Morning Brief here.

Video Transcript

00:00 Speaker A

Goldman Sachs was out with a note yesterday increasing their S&P 500 target to 6600, up from the prior 6100. Now Goldman analyst, David Costin, he cited Fed rate cuts, lower bond yields and investors willingness to look past near-term earning weakness as catalysts for stocks to move higher there. And then this morning, we heard from Bank of America, they also increased their target to 6300, up from the prior 5600. Now, 6300, that implies only about 1% upside based on where we're at at current levels. And the bank said that it's hard to find a catalyst to explain this meteoric rise that we've seen in the S&P 500, but that corporate America might be it. They cited strong transparency there and relatively low earnings uncertainty even amid heightened policy risks. And we've been talking about the low bar heading into earning season. We've had a lot of companies pull guidance. So as long as we can see some beat and raises here, I think that's going to be a good thing for stocks in the long run. So overall, you know, it's interesting to see that these bullish revisions come on the heels of this new tariff uncertainty, these new announcements from President Trump, but it seems to be that the taco trade is alive and well. Markets have largely looked past a lot of what Trump has done. The Trump always chickens out trade that we've been hearing over the past few months. So as long as we see these policy pivots, as long as there's not a significant escalation, we should have a solid setup heading into the back half of the year.

02:55 Speaker B

Well, who are we to say? We'll see what happens on that front, Ali. But, you know, when you look at large cap tech, which as we talked about has been powering the rally from the lows, I was struck by a note that I saw this morning from Stacy Rasgon over at Bernstein. He covers semiconductors and he said, maybe we need to pay attention to tariffs, you know, for some of these industries again. And he says, overall, it remains hard to determine the impact of these new tariffs given we have no idea if they will actually go into effect, how long they will be in effect if they're implemented, or any further changes or alterations to policy that might come down the pipe. And so that obviously affects some of those large cap tech companies in particular, semis, etc. And yet, to your point, we have not seen that effect on the individual stocks.

04:41 Speaker A

Yeah, and Goldman Sachs did cite that as a concern here how we could see tariffs bleed into corporate profits. But I'm looking at the Yahoo Finance interactive right now and we're seeing gains in names like Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, which just started Prime Day today, Meta, Broadcom. So a lot of these names that are exposed to overseas that do have these vulnerabilities if tariffs were to be in place aggressively, they are just rebounding and we just haven't seen that. Another risk could be, you know, bond yields. They're edging a little bit higher today. Obviously, that makes corporate borrowing costs a little more difficult. Now that doesn't fully affect large cap companies, which have pretty solid cash flow levels, but also the small and mid-cap companies could be most exposed. So there's a variety of risks out there in the market right now. But even sources that I've been speaking with have told me that Nvidia is undervalued, that some of these other MAG 7 players are currently relatively valued, that they're not overstretched in any sense of the word. So that surprised me considering that we do have very concentrated pockets of the market. But on a sector basis, we have seen this rally be pretty broad. So that is a positive sign. But with momentum chasing, with FOMO chasing, with everything that we've seen over the past few weeks, there there is that risk that any, you know, stark rise to the top, maybe could lead to a stark rise to the bottom. But according to these Wall Street strategists, that's not something that they see coming in the near term.  Related Videos

title: Meta Poaches Apple AI Executive. What It Means for the Tech Stocks.
content:
Meta Platforms has made another major hire in its push for artificial-intelligence supremacy, this time poaching one of Apple top AI researchers, according to a report Tuesday from The Wall Street Journal. Ruoming Pang, who previously led Apple’s AI and machine-learning foundation model team, will join Meta newly formed Superintelligence Labs unit. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg lured Pang with a pay package worth tens of millions of dollars, the Journal reported.
